Overview

SIRIUS is a desktop and command-line framework for annotating small molecules from high-resolution MS and MS/MS data. It combines isotope-pattern and fragmentation-tree analysis with molecular-formula ranking, CSI:FingerID structure-database searching, compound-class prediction, and confidence estimation.

Detailed capability map

What can this tool do?

Molecular-formula predictionStructure-database searchingStructure elucidationCompound-class predictionSubstructure predictionIdentification-confidence assessmentMS/MS processing

Common uses

  • Rank candidate molecular formulas from isotope and fragmentation patterns.
  • Search molecular-structure databases using predicted fingerprints.
  • Predict compound classes for spectra without confident structure matches.

Scope and considerations

Designed for

  • Molecular-formula and structure-candidate annotation from accurate-mass MS/MS data, including compound-class prediction when exact structures remain uncertain.

Not designed for

  • Primary chromatographic feature detection and alignment; SIRIUS usually receives spectra or feature-associated MS/MS from upstream processing tools.

Important requirements

  • Some functions rely on SIRIUS web services and current access terms; users should consult the official documentation for academic and commercial conditions.

Considerations

  • Candidate rankings are annotations rather than automatic confirmations of chemical identity; confidence and supporting evidence should be reported.
